result: no blockers. `stripCitations` strips only provenance comments, the Claude output is byte-identical, and `verify` and `build` pass.

The built-in `/code-review` did not review the requested range. It reported `6b0a934...HEAD` as empty (it saw HEAD as 953b4d5) and reviewed `6b0a934^2..6b0a934`, so its five findings are about the original Kimi commit, not the repair. I rejected them as outside this range and already covered by the earlier review (`assignment-0mw79mcbn-o9wi`).

The repair was read on HEAD `0e71e52` in `/home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-kimi`; the tree did not change during the review.

- **Markers:** `MARKERS` keeps `<!-- materiality -->` and `<!-- design-core -->`, including indented ones. A test covers this.
- **Claude output:** the Claude sources contain only those two markers and no other comment, so the strip changes nothing there. `mise run build` exited 0, `git status` was clean afterwards, and the diff against the base touches no Claude dist.
- **Pi output:** the build left the committed `pi/dist` unchanged, and it contains no `<!--`. Every Kimi and Claude `SKILL.md` is tested for leftover comments.
- **Unterminated comment:** `a\n<!-- unterminated\nb` comes back unchanged.
- **Tests:** unit tests cover strip, markers and no-op text, plus a `skillFiles` integration test. `CLI_CHECKS` has one entry per family, with the Claude invocations check moved there unchanged.
- **JSDoc:** the stale `PI_FAMILY` JSDoc is fixed.

Optional findings, none blocking:
1. A prose `` `<!--` `` earlier in a file pairs with the next `-->` and deletes the text between them. Probe: ``"a `<!--` x\n```\n<!-- keep? -->\n```\nb --> c"`` returned ``"a `\n```\nb --> c"``. No current source has this pattern. The strip could skip code spans and fences, or this limit could be documented.
2. Adjacent own-line comments leave an extra blank line (`x\n\n\ny`). CRLF sources keep a blank line. Both are cosmetic.
3. Two Kimi role files, `worker-visual/purpose.md` and `method.md`, still carry inline citations. They are not wired to any generator yet, so nothing ships them.
